header.running_head: The Fear of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his Weeping Over Worldly Prosperity

blocks.text: amongst the Sahabah (RA) and said, "It is poverty and hard-living that you fear or are you concerned about the world? Allaah shall certainly grant you conquests over Rome and Persia and worldly wealth will be rained down on you. It will then be nothing but this which will divert you from the straight path."[^1]
The Fear of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and his Weeping Over Worldly Prosperity
The Narration of Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) about the Booty Won at Qaadisiyyah

Hadhrat Miswar bin Makhrama (RA) narrates that when some of the booty won at the Battle of Qaadisiyyah was brought to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he was inspecting it when he began to weep. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) who was with him at the time said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! This is a day of joy and happiness (because we won the battle. Why are you weeping?)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "It certainly is but whenever a nation is given such wealth, they get enmity and hatred along with it."[^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) narrates that when the treasures of the Kisra (Persian Emperor) were brought to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam Zuhri (RA) asked, "Shall we deposit this in the Baytul Maal?" "No," replied Hadhrat Umar (RA), "we shall not deposit it in the Baytul Maal until we have distributed it." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then started to weep. Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) asked, "What makes you weep, O Ameerul Mu'mineen? Today is a day of gratitude and joy." Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Whenever Allaah gives this to a nation, he casts enmity and hatred between them."[^3]
The Narration of Hadhrat Hasan Basri About the Crown of the Kisra

Hadhrat Hasan reports that when the crown of the Kisra was brought before Hadhrat Umar (RA), he placed it before him (together with other crown jewels). Amongst the people was Hadhrat Suraaqa bin Maalik bin Ju'shum (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) threw to him the two bracelets of Kisra bin Hurmuz and when he put them on, they reached up to his shoulders.
